dedupe_keys.name: natural potential for future cropland expansion global index under 2011 2040 climate zabel lmu munich

description: A global raster index of how suitable land that is not cropped today is for expansion of cropland under near-future (2011 to 2040) climate. The Zenodo record says agricultural suitability is derived with a fuzzy logic approach (Zabel et al., 2014) for the 16 most important staple and energy crops, using ECHAM5 climate for the SRES A1B scenario, soils from the Harmonized World Soil Database and SRTM topography, with crop requirements from Sys et al. (1993). The most suitable crop is taken at each pixel, and currently irrigated areas (Siebert et al., 2013) are assumed to stay constant until 2040. Version 1.0 was issued on 4 February 2016 and posted on Zenodo in 2020 by Florian Zabel, as a downloadable GeoTIFF of 62 MB with overview and world files (81 MB in total), free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is global land. Caveats: one climate model and scenario, the spatial resolution is not stated in the record read, and policy limits such as protected areas are discussed but may not be applied. For simulation it indicates where cropland could grow as climate shifts, to test future rural infrastructure and water demand. A related catalogue record is the global agricultural expansion potential maps at 300 m.
